solution.operation: Cross multiply and add (tens × ones + ones × tens)

Multiply the two tens digits straight down, 2 times 1, giving 2 for the hundreds column.

Cross multiply and add: $(2 \times 5) + (4 \times 5) = 10 + 20 = 30$. Add carry-over 2: $30 + 2 = 32$. Write down 2, carry over 3. (Current answer: 20)
Cross multiply and add: $(1 \times 5) + (2 \times 5) + (4 \times 3) = 5 + 10 + 12 = 27$. Add carry-over 3: $27 + 3 = 30$. Write down 0, carry over 3. (Current answer: 020)

concept.technique_name: Criss-Cross step count and step symmetry (2n-1 rule)

examples.problem_statement: The number of steps used for multiplying $n$-digit numbers in the Criss-Cross system is given by $2n-1$. For 2-digit numbers, 3 steps; 3-digit numbers, 5 steps; 4-digit numbers, 7 steps. For 5-digit numbers, how many steps are required? Additionally, if the steps are labeled a, b, c, ..., i, determine which steps are mirror images of each other and which is the central step.

solution.operation: Identify the formula for steps in Criss-Cross multiplication
solution.description: Take the rule stated in the problem as the starting point: multiplying two n-digit numbers by the criss-cross method always takes 2n minus 1 steps.
The question is about 5-digit numbers, so put n equal to 5 in the rule; 2 times 5 minus 1 gives 9 steps.

solution.operation: Label the steps according to the pattern
solution.result: \text{Steps: } a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i
solution.description: Give the nine steps names in order, a through i, so their positions can be compared with each other.

solution.result: a \leftrightarrow i, \, b \leftrightarrow h, \, c \leftrightarrow g, \, d \leftrightarrow f
solution.description: Pair each step with the one an equal distance from the other end: a with i, b with h, c with g, d with f. Each pair uses the same cross pattern reflected.
Only step e is left unpaired; sitting fifth of nine it is the central step, the full-width cross that is its own mirror.

solution.result: \text{For } n=2: 2\times2-1=3 \text{ steps} \\ \text{For } n=3: 2\times3-1=5 \text{ steps} \\ \text{For } n=4: 2\times4-1=7 \text{ steps}
solution.description: Check the rule against the counts already given: n equal to 2 gives 3 steps, n equal to 3 gives 5, and n equal to 4 gives 7, all matching, so 9 for n equal to 5 is safe.

examples.problem_statement: Find the cube root of 64 using the traditional prime factorization method.

solution.description: Begin the prime factorisation of 64 with the smallest prime that divides it, 2, which leaves 32.
32 is still even, so divide by 2 again and record the quotient 16.
16 divided by 2 gives 8; keep peeling off factors of 2 while the quotient stays even.
8 divided by 2 gives 4, with still no odd factor appearing.
4 divided by 2 gives 2, which is itself prime, so the chain of divisions ends here.
Collect every factor pulled out along the way, six 2s in all, so 64 written as a product of primes is 2 to the sixth power.
Taking a cube root divides the exponent by 3, so 2 to the sixth becomes 2 squared, and the cube root of 64 is 4.

examples.problem_statement: Find the cube root of 3375 using the traditional prime factorization method.

solution.description: 3375 ends in 5, so start with the prime 5; dividing gives 675.
675 also ends in 5, so divide by 5 a second time to get 135.
135 still ends in 5, so a third division by 5 leaves 27.
27 is not divisible by 5, so move on to the next prime that fits, 3; dividing 27 by 3 gives 9.
9 is still divisible by 3, so divide again to get 3.
Dividing the remaining 3 by 3 reaches 1, which ends the factorisation.
Write out every prime taken out in order: 3375 is 5 times 5 times 5 times 3 times 3 times 3.
Sort the primes into groups of three identical factors, one group of 5s and one group of 3s, which is exactly the grouping a cube root needs.
Take one factor from each group of three and multiply them, 5 times 3, giving the cube root 15.
